12.text: The whole performance of the Kereˊtkun ceremonial in the

13.text: village of Nuˊnlig̣ren lasts three days, and with most families is

14.text: carried out with the following details. On the first day, in the

15.text: morning, the outer tent is carefully swept, and a net with appur-

16.text: tenances is suspended above. On both sides of the hearth are

17.text: spread reindeer-skins, which represent two inner rooms. The place

18.text: for Kereˊtkun is either on one of these skins, or inside of the

19.text: real sleeping-room. A big lamp filled with the choicest oil is

20.text: lighted, and placed accordingly in either of the indicated places.

21.text: Kereˊtkun is supposed to enter, and, taking his place on the lamp,

22.text: to wait for the sacrifice. He is represented by a small wooden

23.text: image (Fig. 279), which is put on the lamp, and remains there

24.text: till the end of the ceremonial. Opposite the lamp, on a small

25.text: patch of bare ground scraped clean for the purpose, a small fire, which has
